steps.body: Three addends can be grouped in any order. Whichever pair you join first, the total is the same.
steps.narration: Three addends can be grouped in any order. Whichever pair you join first, the total is the same.

widget.prompt: Group 2 + 6 first to get 8, then join 5.
widget.missFeedback: Start at 8 and count on 5: you land on 13.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 13 — the same 13 you reach by grouping any other pair first.

predict.prompt: You group a different pair first. What happens to the total?
predict.reveal: The same three groups are joined either way, so the total cannot change.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1t any order.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for g1t any order must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines g1t any order.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: Regrouping never adds or removes a counter.
Only the ease of the work changes.

widget.prompt: 5 + 3 + 5 = 13. If you group a different pair first, what is the total?

options.label: 13 — the same total
options.feedback: Correct — regrouping changes the order of the work, never the total, so it stays 13.

options.label: 14 — one more
options.feedback: Regrouping moves no counter into the pile, so the total cannot grow past 13.

options.label: 12 — one less
options.feedback: Regrouping takes no counter out of the pile, so the total cannot fall below 13.

options.label: It depends which pair you group
options.feedback: Every grouping of the same three addends reaches the identical total; only the ease changes.

hints: The addends can be grouped in any order.
